references.text: Jacob also watered the sheep at the well, a similar scene at a well where a man helps women with their small livestock.
Abraham's servant met Rebekah at the well, a recurring motif in Scripture where important meetings take place at water sources.
Moses had earlier shown his willingness to defend the oppressed when he struck down the Egyptian; here he continues to protect the weak.
The well as a gathering place for shepherds and small livestock, where the sheep were watered.
The Lord as Savior and Redeemer of His people; Moses' action points forward to God's salvation.
To save the helpless and crush the oppressor, just as Moses defended Jethro's daughters against the shepherds.
Both verses illustrate Moses' role as protector and mediator who intervenes to rescue others from danger.
The candidate provides the necessary context (Moses as a shepherd) to understand the event in the source verse.
